neighbours.label: the continuation piece of a D-initial proper name (Dunk|irk, Di|eter, D|ita, Dic|key)
fire: The novel opens on the beaches of Dunkirk in 1940.
A retrospective of Dieter Rams showed his radios and shelves.
Fans lined up to meet Dita at the burlesque festival.
The film retold the retreat to Dunkirk from a pilot's view.
The poet James Dickey also wrote the novel Deliverance.
The physicist Dieter Zetsche later ran a car company.
Churchill called Dunkirk a miracle of deliverance.
Critics praised Dickey for his raw early poems.
quiet: The novel opens on the beaches of Normandy in 1944.
A retrospective of Charles Eames showed his chairs and shelves.
Fans lined up to meet Bettie at the burlesque festival.
The film retold the retreat to Calais from a pilot's view.
The poet Robert Frost also wrote several plays.
The physicist Werner Heisenberg later ran an institute.
Churchill called Normandy a turning point of the war.
Critics praised Frost for his plain early poems.

notes: Top tokens ' Dunk' x5, 'dic', 'ita', 'eter', 'itt', and Cyrillic д|ик|тат. Probe: Dunkirk 0.80, Dieter 1.08, Dita 0.62, Dickey 0.83, Calais 0.004. A list; the shared pattern seems to be the piece that continues a name split after 'D'/'Di'.
